description: The object-view - the ISO 8.4.3.1.2 Format 5 identifier, `identifier-1 AS { [FACTORY OF] object-class-name-1 [ONLY] | interface-name-1 | UNIVERSAL }` (8.4.3.5.2), which re-describes an object reference at compile time (8.4.3.5.4 GR1) with a run-time conformance check (GR2-GR6, EC-OO-CONFORMANCE). Reachable from every object-reference position (the INVOKE receiver, the inline invocation's receiver, SET Format 5's sender, RAISE), and parsed as a superset in the two object-reference RECEIVING positions so 8.4.3.5.3 SR2 names its own rule (kb/Work PB1425). Gated at 2002 with the rest of the OO CORE. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §2002:8.4.2.5 defines it ('An object-view causes an object reference to be treated as though it had the specified description'), its operand 'shall be of class object' (§2002:8.4.2.5.2 SR1), and §2002:8.4.2.5.3 GR1 reads 'This reference of identifier-1 is treated at compile-time as though it had the description specified by the AS phrase'; COBOL-85 has neither the construct nor its operand: its identifier is a function-identifier or a qualified, subscripted, reference-modified data-name (§1985:IV.4.3.8.5.1 p1: 'An identifier is a syntactically correct sequence of character-strings and separators used to reference data uniquely'), and its data 'are grouped into three classes: alphabetic, numeric, and alphanumeric' (§1985:IV.4.3.3 p1) - no class object; §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 82: 'Object orientation. Support for object oriented programming has been added.' §2014:8.4.2.5 carries the 2002 definition, so 2014 = 2023 (§2023:8.4.3.5.1). Below 2002 the VersionConformancePass parse arm names the edition on RECOGNITION (VisitObjectView -> 0900).
display: object-view identifier AS class / interface / UNIVERSAL
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. OVW.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    CLASS OVWC.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 U USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.
01 C USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE OVWC.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    INVOKE OVWC "NEW" RETURNING U.
    SET C TO U AS OVWC.
    STOP RUN.
END PROGRAM OVW.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
CLASS-ID. OVWC INHERITS FROM BASE.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    CLASS BASE.
END CLASS OVWC.
